artifacts.summary: Implementation summary: per-class finite-axiomatizability verdict, machine-checked soundness/strictness/conditional-completeness, reworded paper footnote.
Canonical per-class verdict record: Σ_fc, four soundness rows, strictness, conditional completeness with ChainComplete explicit.
MinusExt fc Ax closure and the soundness engine minusExt_le_tmFrag.
L⁻ deduction theorem, propositional combinators, and the four □-globality derivations.

completion_data.completion_summary: Established that each H/G-fragment TMFrag fc is finitely axiomatizable over TM⁻ in L⁻ (Σ_Base = (Sp), Σ_ZTime = Z1, Σ_Dense = Σ_RTime = ∅): soundness TM⁻ + Σ_fc ⊆ TMFrag fc at all four classes and strictness TM⁻ ⊊ TM⁻ + Σ_fc at Base/ZTime are machine-checked via the new MinusExt closure, completeness is stated only conditionally on the explicit, never-asserted ChainComplete hypothesis, and the L⁻ deduction theorem plus four □-globality derivations land in MinusDeduction.lean. The paper's negative footnote is reported as not supportable, with reworded text delivered.

memory_candidates.content: For a Type-valued Hilbert derivation tree with a weakening rule, prove the deduction theorem by structural recursion on a subset-generalized statement (Γ' ⊢ φ → Γ' ⊆ A :: Γ → Γ ⊢ A → φ) instead of height-based well-founded recursion: the weakening case becomes a direct recursive call on the sub-derivation, the empty-context rules (necessitation etc.) are handled as theorems weakened under A →, no height lemmas are needed, and with DecidableEq on formulas the result is computable. Propositional combinators (flip, contraposition, DNE, ¬¬-intro) then come cheaply by working in a context and discharging.

When the plan requires a completeness-shaped theorem that is literature-backed but not machine-checkable, encode the classical result as an explicit Prop hypothesis (here ChainComplete fc Ax) and prove the conditional Iff; grep-audit that the hypothesis name appears only in its def, in (h : …) binders, and in prose, so the standing no-sorry-completeness prohibition is preserved while the reduction is still machine-checked.

Mathlib's Lean-4.33-era name for empty-set non-membership is Set.notMem_empty (not Set.not_mem_empty); and the repository's 100-character longLine linter applies inside module docstrings, so wide markdown tables in /-! … -/ blocks must be split into narrow tables plus bullets.

reflection.what_worked: Closing one phase at a time with a scoped guarded build and lean_verify before each commit kept every phase green on the first build except one docstring-linter pass; mirroring the L-side Combinators routes (modalB/modal4) made the S5 derivations mechanical.
reflection.what_was_hard: The plan's deduction-theorem route assumed height lemmas the L⁻ side does not have; the subset-generalized structural recursion resolved it cleanly but had to be recognized as compatible with the plan's decomposition rather than a substitution.
reflection.what_was_missed: The Challenge snapshot was never taken at plan time, so the advisory --check could not run; a plan-time snapshot would have given a mechanical statement-fidelity check for free.
reflection.successes: All 18 Goals identifiers landed sorry-free with axioms within [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]; full build, invariants gate (11 new C14 pins) and cycle check all green; the per-class verdict and the reworded paper footnote are recorded in the canonical module docstring.

next_steps: Reword the PossibleWorlds sub:Logic footnote per the report-back in the summary; optionally take the Challenge snapshot for this task.
